text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Eli Rubinstein, former peacemaker with Egypt and Jordan, is named attorney-general.
- Likud, Labour MPs sign plan for final-status with Palestinians.
- Swiss diplomat terms crisis over Nazi dealings "war".
- Rabbi helps army chief General Amnon Shahak find grandfather's grave in Jerusalem.
- Iscar Ltd Chairman Stef Wertheimer: Privatisation process must placate workers.
- Africa Israel to appoint new executives on Wednesday.
- February monetary policy to be announced at 4.30 p.m. Bankers expect minimal rate decrease.
- Turkey wants more arms deals with Israel, senior Turkish official says.
GLOBES
- Mishtanim and Maof indexes fall 3.6 percent because of attorney-general affair, decline on Wall Street and concerns about interest rate decision today.
- Interest rate drop of up to 0.5 percent expected.
HAARETZ
- Syrian ambassador to Washington says Damascus will be ready to resume talks with Israel after Secretary of State Madeleine Albright visits Damascus.
MAARIV
- Reserve Brigadier-General David Agmon intends to quit his job as head of the prime minister's bureau, feeling his talents not being put to their full potential.
- 70 percent of Israelis are in permanent overdraft.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat: I'll declare a state only after the final-status agreement.
